# zstd / fse_read_ncount

zstd's own fuzz target `fse_read_ncount` ([source](source/fse_read_ncount.c), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over zstd (facebook/zstd at 82d322c4).

Checks 2 properties (listed below); the first, a round trip: Build a random valid FSE normalized count (sum = 1<<tableLog), FSE_writeNCount it, append random trailing bytes, FSE_readNCount: must succeed, consume exactly the written size, and return the same maxSymbolValue, tableLog and every count.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against zstd at commit 82d322c4.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- FSE_writeNCount must succeed within FSE_NCountWriteBound ([lines 62-66](source/fse_read_ncount.c#L62-L66)): abort(); confirmed in the binary.
- Build a random valid FSE normalized count (sum = 1<<tableLog), FSE_writeNCount it, append random trailing bytes, FSE_readNCount: must succeed, consume exactly the written size, and return the same maxSymbolValue, tableLog and every count ([lines 84-94](source/fse_read_ncount.c#L84-L94)): abort(); confirmed in the binary.

A failed check marked as ending the process contradicts every halts statement below, so a proof of one implies them on every input it covers.
